questions.stem: One square metre is equal to:
questions.explanation: A square metre is 100 cm by 100 cm, so it holds 100 × 100 = 10 000 cm². Using 100 converts the length but forgets that area has two dimensions.

questions.stem: A capacity of one litre is equal to a volume of:
questions.explanation: One millilitre is 1 cm³, and a litre is 1000 mL, so 1 L = 1000 cm³. One cubic metre is much larger: 1000 L.

questions.stem: The number 0.004 05 has how many significant figures?
questions.explanation: Leading zeros only place the decimal point and are not significant. The figures 4, 0 and 5 are significant, because the zero lies between non-zero digits.

questions.stem: In scientific notation, 0.000 62 is written as:
questions.explanation: The decimal point moves 4 places right to give 6.2, so the power is −4. The form 62 × 10⁻⁵ has the right value but is not scientific notation, which needs a number from 1 to less than 10.

questions.stem: Two shapes are similar when:
options: corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are in the same ratio
corresponding sides are equal and their angles may differ
they have the same area and the same perimeter
they have the same number of sides and the same area
questions.explanation: Similar shapes are enlargements of each other: the same shape, with every length multiplied by the same scale factor. Equal sides and angles would make them congruent, a special case.

questions.stem: The area of a sector with radius r and angle θ° at the centre is:
questions.explanation: A sector is the fraction θ/360 of the whole circle, so its area is that fraction of πr². The expression (θ/360) × 2πr is the arc length.

questions.stem: The volume of a pyramid with base area A and height h is:
questions.explanation: A pyramid holds one-third of the prism with the same base and height, so V = (1/3)Ah. The formula Ah is for the prism.

questions.stem: In a right-angled triangle, sin θ is equal to:
questions.explanation: SOH: sine is opposite over hypotenuse. Adjacent over hypotenuse is cosine, and opposite over adjacent is tangent.

questions.stem: The three-figure (true) bearing of due west is:
questions.explanation: True bearings are measured clockwise from north: east is 090°T, south 180°T and west 270°T.

questions.stem: An angle of elevation is measured:
questions.explanation: An angle of elevation is the angle up from the horizontal to an object above the observer. An angle of depression is measured down from the horizontal.

questions.stem: In triangle ABC, with side a opposite angle A, the cosine rule states:
questions.explanation: The cosine rule is a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A. When A = 90°, cos A = 0 and it becomes Pythagoras’ theorem, which is why it is called a generalisation of that theorem.

questions.stem: In triangle ABC, with sides a, b and c opposite angles A, B and C, the sine rule states:
options: a sin A = b sin B = c sin C
sin A/b = sin B/c = sin C/a
a/sin B = b/sin C = c/sin A
a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C
questions.explanation: Each side divided by the sine of its opposite angle gives the same value. The rule pairs every side with the angle opposite it, not a neighbouring angle.

questions.stem: In a non-right-angled triangle all three sides are known. To find an angle, use:
questions.explanation: With three sides and no angles, the sine rule has no side–angle pair to start from, but the cosine rule rearranges to give an angle directly. Pythagoras and tangent apply only to right-angled triangles.

questions.stem: The number 0.072 85 correct to two significant figures is:
questions.explanation: The first two significant figures are 7 and 2. The next digit, 8, rounds the 2 up, giving 0.073. The value 0.07 has only one significant figure.

questions.stem: A volume of 2.5 m³ is equal to a capacity of:
questions.explanation: One cubic metre is 1000 L, so 2.5 m³ = 2.5 × 1000 = 2500 L.

questions.stem: A triangle has sides 8 cm and 11 cm with an included angle of 30°. Its area is:
questions.explanation: Area = (1/2)ab sin C = 0.5 × 8 × 11 × sin 30° = 0.5 × 88 × 0.5 = 22 cm². Leaving out the 1/2 gives 44 cm².

questions.stem: Using Heron’s formula, the area of a triangle with sides 5 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm is:
questions.explanation: The semi-perimeter is s = 8, so A = √(8 × 3 × 3 × 2) = √144 = 12 cm². The value 24 forgets the 1/2 in base × height, where the height to the 6 cm side is 4 cm.

questions.stem: The area of a sector with radius 6 cm and angle 60° at the centre is:
questions.explanation: The sector is 60/360 = 1/6 of the circle, so its area is (1/6) × π × 6² = 6π ≈ 18.85 cm². The value 2π is the arc length, and 36π is the whole circle.

questions.stem: The length of an arc of a circle with radius 10 cm and angle 72° at the centre is:
questions.explanation: The arc is 72/360 = 1/5 of the circumference, so its length is (1/5) × 2π × 10 = 4π ≈ 12.57 cm. The value 20π is the area of the sector, not its arc.

questions.stem: The volume of a cylinder with radius 3 cm and height 10 cm is:
questions.explanation: V = πr²h = π × 9 × 10 = 90π ≈ 282.7 cm³. The value 60π uses 2πrh, the curved surface area, not the volume.

questions.stem: The surface area of a sphere with radius 5 cm is:
questions.explanation: The surface area is 4πr² = 4π × 25 = 100π ≈ 314.2 cm². The value (500/3)π is the volume, (4/3)πr³.

questions.stem: The volume of a sphere with radius 3 m is:
questions.explanation: V = (4/3)πr³ = (4/3) × π × 27 = 36π ≈ 113.1 m³. Forgetting the 1/3 gives 108π, and 27π leaves out the 4/3 altogether.

questions.stem: A garden bed is a 10 m by 6 m rectangle with a semicircle on one 6 m side. Its area is:
questions.explanation: The semicircle has radius 3 m, so its area is 0.5 × π × 9 ≈ 14.14 m². Adding the 60 m² rectangle gives 74.14 m². Using a full circle of radius 3 m gives 88.27 m².

questions.stem: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides of 4 cm and 10 cm. The smaller triangle has area 12 cm². The area of the larger is:
questions.explanation: The length scale factor is k = 10/4 = 2.5, so areas scale by k² = 6.25: 12 × 6.25 = 75 cm². Multiplying by 2.5 alone gives 30 cm², which treats area like length.

questions.stem: A triangular prism has a triangular face with base 6 cm and height 4 cm, and is 10 cm long. Its volume is:
questions.explanation: V = area of the cross-section × length = (0.5 × 6 × 4) × 10 = 12 × 10 = 120 cm³. Forgetting the 1/2 in the triangle’s area gives 240 cm³.

questions.stem: Which information is enough to show that two triangles are similar?
options: one pair of corresponding angles is equal
one pair of corresponding sides is equal
the two triangles have equal perimeters
two pairs of corresponding angles are equal
questions.explanation: If two pairs of angles match, the third pair must too, since the angles add to 180°, so the triangles are similar (AAA). One matching angle or one matching side is not enough.

questions.stem: For any angle θ between 0° and 180°, sin(180° − θ) is equal to:
questions.explanation: An angle and its supplement have the same sine, so sin 150° = sin 30° = 0.5. This is the source of the ambiguous case of the sine rule. Cosines of supplements have opposite signs instead.

questions.stem: The value of cos 120° is:
questions.explanation: cos 120° = −cos 60° = −0.5: the cosine of an obtuse angle is negative. Giving 0.5 forgets the sign change.

questions.stem: A 5 m ladder leans against a vertical wall with its foot 1.4 m from the wall. How high up the wall does it reach?
questions.explanation: The ladder is the hypotenuse: h² = 5² − 1.4² = 25 − 1.96 = 23.04, so h = 4.8 m. Adding the squares gives 5.2 m, which would make the wall height longer than the ladder.

questions.stem: From a point 30 m from the base of a tree, the angle of elevation to its top is 40°. The height of the tree is about:
questions.explanation: The height is opposite the 40° angle and the 30 m distance is adjacent, so h = 30 tan 40° ≈ 25.2 m. Using sine instead gives 19.3 m.

questions.stem: In a right-angled triangle, the side opposite angle θ is 7 cm and the side adjacent to it is 10 cm. θ is about:
questions.explanation: tan θ = 7/10 = 0.7, so θ = tan⁻¹ 0.7 ≈ 35.0°. Using sin⁻¹ 0.7 gives 44.4°, but 10 cm is not the hypotenuse. The value 55.0° is the other acute angle.

questions.stem: Town B is on a bearing of 060°T from town A. The bearing of A from B is:
questions.explanation: The return direction is opposite, so add 180°: 060° + 180° = 240°T. Subtracting from 180° gives 120°T, which is not the reverse direction.

questions.stem: In triangle ABC, A = 40°, B = 65° and a = 10 cm. Side b, to one decimal place, is:
questions.explanation: By the sine rule, b = a sin B / sin A = 10 × sin 65° / sin 40° ≈ 14.1 cm. Inverting the ratio, 10 sin 40° / sin 65°, gives 7.1 cm, which is too short for the side opposite the larger angle.

questions.stem: In triangle ABC, b = 7 cm, c = 9 cm and A = 60°. Side a, to two decimal places, is:
questions.explanation: a² = 7² + 9² − 2 × 7 × 9 × cos 60° = 49 + 81 − 63 = 67, so a ≈ 8.19 cm. Leaving out the cos term gives √130 ≈ 11.40, and adding it gives √193 ≈ 13.89.

questions.stem: A model of a water tank is built to a scale of 1 : 50. The real tank holds 250 m³. The model holds:
questions.explanation: Volumes scale by the cube of the length scale factor: 250 ÷ 50³ = 250 ÷ 125 000 = 0.002 m³, which is 2 L. Dividing by 50 treats volume like length, and dividing by 2500 treats it like area.

questions.stem: A box measures 3 cm by 4 cm by 12 cm. The length of the longest straight rod that fits inside it is:
questions.explanation: The diagonal of the 3 by 4 base is 5 cm. The space diagonal is then √(5² + 12²) = √169 = 13 cm, which is Pythagoras’ theorem used twice. The value 5 cm is only the base diagonal.

questions.stem: A square-based pyramid has base side 10 cm and vertical height 12 cm. Its total surface area is:
questions.explanation: The slant height of each triangular face is √(12² + 5²) = 13 cm, so the four faces have area 4 × 0.5 × 10 × 13 = 260 cm². Adding the 100 cm² base gives 360 cm². Using 12 cm as the slant height gives 340 cm².

questions.stem: Two similar cylinders have volumes 16 cm³ and 54 cm³. The smaller has surface area 36 cm². The surface area of the larger is:
questions.explanation: The volume ratio 54/16 = 27/8 = k³, so k = 3/2 and the area ratio is k² = 9/4. The larger surface area is 36 × 9/4 = 81 cm². Using the volume ratio directly gives 121.5 cm².

questions.stem: From the top of an 80 m cliff, the angle of depression to a boat is 25°. The distance from the base of the cliff to the boat is about:
questions.explanation: The angle of elevation from the boat to the clifftop equals the 25° angle of depression, so tan 25° = 80/d and d = 80 ÷ tan 25° ≈ 171.6 m. Multiplying instead, 80 tan 25°, gives 37.3 m.

questions.stem: A hiker walks 5 km north and then 12 km east. The bearing of the hiker’s finishing point from the start is:
questions.explanation: The angle east of north satisfies tan θ = 12/5, so θ ≈ 67.4° and the bearing is 067°T. The value 023°T measures the angle from east rather than from north, and 247°T is the bearing back to the start.

questions.stem: A triangle has sides 5 cm, 7 cm and 8 cm. The angle opposite the 7 cm side is:
questions.explanation: cos θ = (5² + 8² − 7²) ÷ (2 × 5 × 8) = 40 ÷ 80 = 0.5, so θ = 60°. The values 38.2° and 81.8° are the angles opposite the 5 cm and 8 cm sides.

questions.stem: In triangle ABC, A = 30°, a = 6 cm and b = 10 cm. The possible values of B are:
questions.explanation: sin B = 10 sin 30° / 6 ≈ 0.833, so B ≈ 56.4° or 180° − 56.4° = 123.6°. Both work, since 30° + 123.6° < 180°. This is the ambiguous case of the sine rule.

questions.stem: In triangle ABC, A = 30°, b = 10 cm and a = 4 cm. How many triangles fit this information?
questions.explanation: The sine rule gives sin B = 10 sin 30° / 4 = 1.25, which is impossible because a sine cannot exceed 1. Side a is too short to reach the third side.

questions.stem: A ship sails 8 km on a bearing of 040°T, then 5 km on a bearing of 100°T. Its distance from the start is about:
questions.explanation: The turn makes an angle of 180° − 60° = 120° between the two legs, so d² = 8² + 5² − 2 × 8 × 5 × cos 120° = 89 + 40 = 129 and d ≈ 11.4 km. Using 60° as the angle gives 7.0 km.
